t: IP Address Planner - public implementations survey
title: IP Address Planner - public implementations survey
definition: Allocates address ranges for a proposed network.
description:
IP Address Planner is one of the fundamental capabilities an AI needs to build things on demand: Allocates address ranges for a proposed network. In the real world this capability is delivered by a rich ecosystem of tools, libraries and platforms. This database is the public edition - a fact-checked survey of the real implementations, the real techniques they share, the standards they follow, and laddered drills that teach the capability hands-on.

No single tool owns IP Address Planner. Competing implementations emphasize different trade-offs: speed against flexibility, simplicity against power, integration against independence. The implementation spotlights in this database document the notable real ones - what each does, where it excels, and how it serves IP Address Planner. Together they map the territory as it actually exists.

Every record carries a runnable demonstration program, because tools are understood by use. Run the demos with node, compare the implementations, practice the drills, and the IP Address Planner capability becomes something you can reach for - with full knowledge of which real tool fits which job.

t: TCP/IP - related IP Address Planner technology
title: TCP/IP - related IP Address Planner technology
definition: The internet's packet protocols.
description:
TCP/IP is not itself an IP Address Planner, but it belongs in this survey because real IP Address Planner work leans on it. The internet's packet protocols.

In an IP Address Planner build it shows up when startup speed beats raw peak power. Its architecture reflects hard-won lessons: small sharp pieces, explicit contracts between them, and no magic hidden from the operator. Knowing the surrounding technology is part of knowing the capability - the best IP Address Planner practitioners can say exactly where their tool ends and its neighbors begin.

For builders, TCP/IP is a solid foundation to build on as supporting technology. The demo program exercises a core idea from its domain - run it with node and watch each step.
